items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Buster got there in time to open up in Roseland, so we had a full band then.

ctx.x: Well, he adjusted to that right away, because he had music in him. It was just a different horn, that was all. And so that made the band a little more even, three trumpets. So we continued and continued. In the meantime, there were rumors going around about Duke. Well, I didn't know what they meant and everything. And Fletcher -- oh, Louis came first. I was so busy talking about Louis I forgot about Buster.
Buster got there in time to open up in Roseland, so we had a full band then. Before that, it had just been Don Readman and Coleman Hawkins. Now, that made a trio then, and he
was excellent on that clarinet. Well, musicians came from far and wide just to see his band. But Duke was coming up, slowly but surely.
